svg.text: For kitchen equipment, exhaust, gas, plumbing and electrical vendors · plan at 1:25 and elevation at 1:40 on A3

Legend: every symbol and letter on this sheet
drain line to the grease trap
hot water pipe from heater W
P1 to P14 power point (services list); plain numbers 1 to 44 are BOQ items
K Class K extinguisher (wok and fryer fires)
SP hood suppression pull + gas cut-off
P1, P2 structural pillars on the right wall
E, F, CC, G, WC, SU, PF: services list
Duct along the wall, round the corner

35 L · left wall over the sink
left wall over the DW · on backup
Allow about 4,000–5,000 m³/h for the whole hood (vendor to size);
about 8 m/s in the 0.40 × 0.40 duct. ESP + carbon filter before
the fan. No roof stack: apartment above, parking behind.
Hood overhang 0.20 m at the open end, 0.15 m over the wok range.
Make-up air about 80% of the exhaust through two low-velocity
diffusers (~2.4 m/s), cooled by a 1.5 TR coil, interlocked.
5 × 19 kg LPG (4 on the manifold + 1 full spare = 95 kg) in a
locked cage on the right strip. Typical load: wok 2 × 18, stock
2 × 8, fryer 18, steamer 11 kW = about 80 kW connected, 55 kW
at once; 4 cylinders give about 60–75 kW in Goa: vendor to
confirm the burner ratings, add a vaporiser if they are higher.
A valve per appliance; solenoid shuts off with the fan or the
suppression; leak detector low on the right wall.
Cold: 1,000 L buried sump → pump, filter, softener cabinet
(on backup) → kitchen. Hot: 35 L heater for the sink and pre-
rinse, 6 L heaters under both hand-wash basins, dishwasher
with its own booster. All kitchen drains to the grease trap,
then the grey-water line (never the biodigester).
Shop supply: three-phase, about 15–20 kW. Backup 7.5 kVA
covers the fridges, rails, fan, ESP, lights and the water pump.
